description: The Royal Enfield Classic 350 is a retro-styled modern cruiser powered by the refined J-series 349cc single-cylinder engine. Known for its thumping exhaust note, relaxed upright ergonomics, and planted highway stability, it excels in comfortable city commuting and weekend touring.
pros: Refined J-series engine with minimal vibrations; iconic retro styling; comfortable upright riding posture; strong low-end torque.
cons: Heavy kerb weight makes tight parking tricky; lacks a 6th gear for high-speed cruising; basic instrument cluster.

description: The Yamaha R15 V4 is an entry-level track-focused supersport motorcycle featuring Variable Valve Actuation (VVA), upside-down front forks, traction control, and a quickshifter. Its aerodynamic fairing and aggressive clip-on handlebars deliver sharp cornering dynamics.
pros: Razor-sharp handling and Deltabox frame stability; high-revving VVA engine; traction control and quickshifter; impressive fuel efficiency.
cons: Aggressive committed riding posture causes wrist fatigue in traffic; cramped pillion seat; expensive for a 155cc bike.

description: The KTM 390 Duke is an aggressive naked streetfighter built for explosive acceleration and agile street performance. Equipped with a 398cc LC4c engine, ride-by-wire throttle, cornering ABS, launch control, and a 5-inch TFT display, it offers unmatched tech in its class.
pros: Thrilling power-to-weight ratio; class-leading electronics including cornering ABS and quickshifter+; adjustable WP Apex suspension.
cons: Engine heat noticeable in bumper-to-bumper traffic; stiff suspension setup on broken roads; high maintenance costs.

description: The Hero Splendor Plus is India's quintessential everyday commuter motorcycle, celebrated for bulletproof reliability, ultra-low maintenance, and exceptional fuel economy. Its lightweight chassis and long flat seat make it ideal for daily utility and rural or urban travel.
pros: Exceptional fuel efficiency exceeding 65-70 kmpl; rock-solid reliability and widespread service network; lightweight and easy to maneuver.
cons: Lacks modern safety features like ABS; basic drum brakes; limited highway capability above 70 km/h.

description: The Royal Enfield Himalayan 450 is a purpose-built adventure tourer powered by the liquid-cooled Sherpa 450 engine. Featuring long-travel Showa USD forks, a 21-inch front spoke wheel, switchable rear ABS, and a circular TFT Tripper Dash with Google Maps integration, it conquers rugged terrain.
pros: Plush long-travel suspension absorbs potholes and trails effortlessly; strong mid-range torque; integrated Google Maps navigation.
cons: Top-heavy feel at low speeds; tubed tires on standard spoke wheels; tall seat height for shorter riders.

description: The Bajaj Pulsar NS200 is a muscular streetfighter sporting a perimeter frame, liquid-cooled triple-spark 4-valve engine, and upside-down front forks. It balances everyday practicality with spirited high-RPM performance at an accessible price point.
pros: Punchy top-end performance; solid high-speed stability from the perimeter frame; great value-for-money pricing.
cons: Dated muscular design silhouette; slight vibrations near the redline; firm seat cushioning on long rides.

description: The TVS Apache RTR 160 4V is a sporty 160cc commuter-streetfighter offering three ride modes (Urban, Rain, Sport), Glide Through Technology (GTT) for effortless traffic crawling, and a throaty exhaust note.
pros: Best-in-class refinement and throttle response; multiple ride modes; agile handling for city filtering.
cons: Missing a 6th gear for relaxed highway cruising; rear seat space is moderate for two-up touring.

description: The Honda H'ness CB350 blends classic roadster aesthetics with Honda's trademark refinement. It features an assist-and-slipper clutch, Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC), all-LED lighting, and a deep, bass-heavy exhaust note.
pros: Silky-smooth engine refinement and light clutch action; traction control standard; comfortable ergonomics for rider and pillion.
cons: Tall gearing requires frequent downshifts in slow traffic; sold exclusively through BigWing dealerships.

description: The Triumph Speed 400 brings British neo-retro roadster styling to the 400cc segment. Powered by a liquid-cooled TR-series engine with 43mm golden USD forks, switchable traction control, and premium fit-and-finish, it combines daily usability with brisk performance.
pros: Top-notch paint quality and fit-and-finish; tractable low-to-mid-range torque; accessible 790mm seat height; long 16,000 km service intervals.
cons: Buzziness felt in handlebars above 110 km/h; semi-digital cluster lacks turn-by-turn navigation.

description: The Kawasaki Ninja 300 is a parallel-twin entry-level sports tourer famed for its high-revving 13,000 RPM redline, turbine-like smoothness, and forgiving sport-touring ergonomics that welcome both beginners and highway riders.
pros: Refined parallel-twin engine with linear power delivery; comfortable sport-touring ergonomics; large 17-liter fuel tank.
cons: Dated halogen headlights and analog-digital instrument cluster; lacks USD forks and modern rider aids.

description: The Yamaha MT-15 V2 strips down the R15 into an agile hyper-naked streetfighter. With wide handlebars, a featherlight 141 kg kerb weight, USD front forks, and traction control, it is built for effortless urban flickability.
pros: Ultra-light and nimble in dense city traffic; peppy VVA engine with strong fuel economy; aggressive streetfighter styling.
cons: Very small pillion seat; stiff rear monoshock on sharp bumps; premium price tag.

description: The Bajaj Dominar 400 is a factory-accessorized power cruiser and highway tourer equipped with a tall windscreen, hand guards, engine bash plate, luggage rack, and a 373cc liquid-cooled engine designed for sustained triple-digit cruising.
pros: Comes standard with touring accessories; planted highway stability; strong mid-range pull.
cons: Heavy 193 kg weight and wide turning radius in tight city streets; 13-liter fuel tank limits highway range.

description: The Hero Xpulse 200 4V is an accessible dual-sport motorcycle designed for trail riding, off-road exploration, and rough daily commutes. Featuring 21-inch front and 18-inch rear spoked wheels, 220mm ground clearance, and three ABS modes (Road, Off-road, Rally), it is the ideal entry point into off-roading.
pros: Unmatched off-road capability and value for money; lightweight and easy to pick up on trails; forgiving long-travel suspension.
cons: Lacks top-end power for fast highway overtakes; tubed tires require puncture preparation; tall seat height.

description: The Royal Enfield Continental GT 650 is an authentic cafe racer powered by a characterful 648cc parallel-twin engine with a 270-degree crank. Featuring clip-on handlebars, rear-set footpegs, and twin upswept exhausts, it delivers classic style and effortless twin-cylinder torque.
pros: Creamy, torquey 648cc parallel-twin engine; timeless cafe racer design; dual-channel ABS and slipper clutch.
cons: Heavy 211 kg kerb weight; committed cafe racer posture strains wrists on long journeys; small 12.5-liter tank.

description: The Suzuki Gixxer SF 250 is a fully-faired quarter-liter sports tourer utilizing Suzuki's Oil Cooling System (SOCS). It pairs comfortable clip-on ergonomics with a tractable, vibration-free 249cc engine suited for both daily commuting and weekend highway runs.
pros: Refined and reliable SOCS engine; comfortable sport-touring ergonomics; sharp handling and strong braking.
cons: Basic LCD instrument console; firm rear suspension; understated exhaust note.

description: The TVS Ronin is a genre-blending modern-retro neo-scrambler combining cruiser comfort with scrambler styling. Equipped with Showa 41mm USD forks, an offset digital speedometer with Bluetooth connectivity, and a silent starter, it prioritizes relaxed urban cruising.
pros: Tractable low-end torque ideal for city riding; plush suspension; feature-rich with GTT and dual ABS modes.
cons: Top-end highway performance tapers off past 105 km/h; wide turning radius.

description: The Honda Shine 125 is a benchmark 125cc executive commuter renowned for its silent ACG starter, whisper-quiet eSP engine, and smooth 5-speed gearbox. It delivers stress-free daily commuting with strong resale value.
pros: Ultra-refined and silent 125cc engine; smooth 5-speed transmission; high 60 kmpl fuel efficiency.
cons: Conservative styling; narrow rear tire limits cornering grip; lacks digital console or ABS.

description: The Aprilia RS 457 is an Italian twin-cylinder supersport built around a lightweight aluminum twin-spar frame. Featuring a 270-degree crank parallel-twin engine, three ride modes, three-level traction control, and MotoGP-inspired aerodynamics, it sets the benchmark in the sub-500cc sportbike class.
pros: Exotic aluminum frame and segment-best power-to-weight ratio; thrilling parallel-twin exhaust note; comprehensive electronics suite.
cons: Quickshifter is an optional extra; firm suspension tuned for smooth tarmac; limited service network outside major metros.

description: The Harley-Davidson X440 is an accessible American-inspired roadster co-developed with Hero MotoCorp. Its long-stroke 440cc engine delivers a deep, bassy exhaust rumble and massive low-end torque starting from 2,000 RPM, paired with KYB USD forks and a TFT display.
pros: Effortless low-end torque for city and highway cruising; authentic deep exhaust note; neutral, commanding ergonomics.
cons: Exposed wiring and weld finishes on lower variants; noticeable vibrations above 4,500 RPM.

description: The Ather 450X is a high-performance smart electric scooter featuring an aluminum chassis, instant 26 Nm electric torque, Warp mode acceleration, a 7-inch touchscreen dashboard with Google Maps, and a real-world certified range of 110 km per charge.
pros: Instantaneous throttle response in Warp mode; sharp handling with low center of gravity; intuitive touchscreen UI and fast charging network.
cons: Firm suspension over deep potholes; Pro Pack features require additional upfront cost; limited under-seat boot space compared to rivals.

description: The Yamaha FZ-S Fi V4 is a muscular 150cc street commuter featuring traction control, Bluetooth Y-Connect, LED lighting, and a lightweight 136 kg chassis tailored for comfortable daily urban rides.
pros: Lightweight and flickable in city traffic; refined engine with good mileage; traction control in a 150cc commuter.
cons: Modest 12.4 bhp power output; single-channel ABS only.

description: The Bajaj Platina 110 ABS is a comfort-focused budget commuter featuring long-travel spring-on-spring suspension, a plush quilted seat, and segment-first single-channel ABS for enhanced safety.
pros: Segment-first ABS in the 110cc commuter category; plush suspension absorbs bad roads; high 70 kmpl mileage.
cons: Basic styling; modest top speed around 85 km/h.

description: The Royal Enfield Hunter 350 is a compact, agile urban roadster utilizing the 349cc J-series engine with 17-inch alloy wheels and tighter steering geometry for nimble city maneuverability.
pros: 14 kg lighter and much more agile than the Classic 350; accessible price and 790mm seat height; punchy urban torque.
cons: Stiff rear suspension on sharp bumps; limited highway wind protection.

description: The KTM 390 Adventure is a lightweight rally-inspired adventure tourer equipped with cornering traction control, off-road ABS, a bidirectional quickshifter, and a 373cc engine built for high-speed highway and trail touring.
pros: Thrilling highway performance and lightweight agility; advanced cornering electronics; crisp TFT display.
cons: Tall 855mm seat height intimidates shorter riders; weak low-end torque requires clutch modulation off-road.

description: The TVS Raider 125 is a youthful 125cc sporty commuter offering brisk acceleration, under-seat storage, Eco and Power ride modes, and a reverse LCD instrument cluster.
pros: Peppy 3-valve engine with strong mid-range; comfortable split-seat setup; great fuel economy.
cons: Lacks single-channel ABS; firm suspension on rough patches.

description: The Suzuki V-Strom SX 250 is a lightweight sport-adventure tourer featuring a 19-inch front wheel, tall windscreen, knuckle covers, rear luggage rack, and Suzuki's smooth 249cc oil-cooled engine.
pros: Comfortable upright touring ergonomics; refined and reliable 250cc engine; lightweight and easy to handle.
cons: Short-travel street-biased suspension; 12-liter fuel tank is small for long-distance touring.

description: The Honda Hornet 2.0 is a muscular 184cc streetfighter equipped with golden upside-down front forks, an assist-and-slipper clutch, tank-mounted ignition key, and crisp low-end acceleration.
pros: Refined Honda engine with punchy city acceleration; light slipper clutch; sharp USD fork styling.
cons: Stiff rear suspension; lacks dual-channel ABS and a 6th gear.

description: The Bajaj Chetak is a neo-retro electric scooter built with an all-metal steel body, IP67 water resistance, smooth linear throttle calibration, and a certified range of 123 km.
pros: Sturdy all-metal build quality; smooth, predictable throttle response; trusted nationwide service support.
cons: Slower charging times compared to fast-charging rivals; modest top speed of 63-73 km/h.

description: The Royal Enfield Interceptor 650 is a classic British-style roadster featuring upright handlebars, a flat bench seat, and the acclaimed 648cc parallel-twin engine that delivers smooth highway cruising.
pros: Characterful and smooth 648cc twin engine; comfortable upright riding position; great value for a twin-cylinder bike.
cons: Heavy kerb weight; flat seat can become uncomfortable over 200 km without touring upgrades.

description: The Kawasaki Z900 is an inline-four supernaked motorcycle delivering intoxicating 4-cylinder exhaust acoustics, 125 bhp of seamless power, traction control, riding modes, and aggressive Sugomi styling.
pros: Silky-smooth inline-four engine with immense torque; manageable seat height for a big bike; aggressive street presence.
cons: Lacks a standard bidirectional quickshifter; heavy weight in tight U-turns.

description: The BMW G 310 GS is an entry-level luxury adventure tourer featuring a reverse-inclined 313cc engine, plush long-travel suspension, ride-by-wire throttle, and unmistakable GS styling.
pros: Plush suspension comfort on broken roads; aspirational BMW badge and GS ergonomics; light clutch.
cons: High service and spare parts costs; small 11.5-liter fuel tank; engine buzz at highway speeds.

description: The Jawa 42 Bobber is a factory-custom single-seater bobber featuring a floating solo saddle, chopped fenders, bar-end mirrors, and a liquid-cooled 334cc engine with strong mid-range pull.
pros: Head-turning factory bobber styling; ultra-low 740mm seat height; punchy 6-speed liquid-cooled engine.
cons: Strictly a single-seater with no pillion option; limited ground clearance over tall speed breakers.

description: The Yezdi Scrambler is a rugged retro-scrambler equipped with twin upswept exhausts, a beak-style front fender, 19-inch front wheel, and three ABS modes (Road, Off-road, Rain) for urban and trail versatility.
pros: Authentic scrambler looks with twin exhausts; punchy mid-range performance; switchable ABS modes.
cons: Firm rear suspension; engine heat felt in slow-moving traffic.

description: The TVS Apache RR 310 is a wind-tunnel-tested supersport featuring aerodynamic winglets, a vertical 5-inch TFT display, four ride modes (Track, Sport, Urban, Rain), and sharp chassis balance.
pros: Loaded with segment-first tech including cruise control and cornering ABS; sharp aerodynamic styling; versatile riding modes.
cons: Noticeable engine vibrations above 6,500 RPM; firm seat for long rides.

description: The Hero Mavrick 440 is a muscular roadster powered by a torquey 440cc engine, offering plush suspension tuning, a steel trellis frame, e-SIM connectivity, and effortless highway cruising.
pros: Plush ride quality over rough roads; meaty low-end torque; competitive pricing for a 440cc roadster.
cons: Understated styling compared to rivals; basic negative LCD display.

description: The Bajaj Freedom 125 is the world's first dual-fuel CNG and petrol motorcycle, housing a 2 kg CNG cylinder integrated safely inside a trellis frame alongside a 2-liter auxiliary petrol tank, delivering over 330 km combined range at half the running cost.
pros: Ultra-low running cost with 102 km/kg CNG efficiency; seamless switch between CNG and petrol; long flat seat.
cons: Heavy 149 kg kerb weight for a 125cc commuter; modest acceleration in CNG mode.

description: The Honda CB300R is an ultra-lightweight Neo-Sports Cafe roadster weighing just 146 kg. Powered by a rev-happy 286cc liquid-cooled engine with IMU-based dual-channel ABS and USD forks, it offers explosive agility.
pros: Featherlight 146 kg kerb weight yields razor-sharp agility; refined and rev-happy engine; premium Neo-Sports Cafe design.
cons: Small 9.7-liter fuel tank restricts touring range; cramped pillion seat.

description: The Ola S1 Pro Gen 2 is a high-range smart electric scooter powered by an 11 kW peak motor and a 4 kWh battery pack, offering a 120 km/h top speed, cruise control, Hyper mode, and 195 km IDC range.
pros: Thrilling acceleration and 120 km/h top speed; large 34-liter under-seat storage; strong real-world range.
cons: After-sales service bottlenecks in certain regions; touchscreen-dependent controls.

description: The Triumph Scrambler 400 X builds on the Speed 400 platform with a 19-inch front wheel, longer-travel suspension, wider handlebars, headlight grille, and switchable off-road ABS for light trail adventures.
pros: Commanding riding posture and plush suspension; premium fit-and-finish; versatile on both tarmac and gravel.
cons: Tall 835mm seat height; high-speed handlebar buzz past 115 km/h.

description: The Ducati Panigale V4 is a flagship MotoGP-derived superbike powered by the 1,103cc Desmosedici Stradale V4 engine. Equipped with biplane aerodynamic wings, slide control, wheelie control, and Brembo Stylema brakes, it is built for pure racetrack dominance.
pros: Blistering 215.5 bhp V4 performance; cutting-edge electronic rider aids; breathtaking Italian aerodynamic design.
cons: Extreme engine heat in city traffic; super-aggressive track ergonomics; high purchase and maintenance cost.
